subject: Urgent: 72-hour notice request — limited-scope telemetry exposure & subprocessor assistance
messages:
From: Jake Morris <jake.morris@finlytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finlytics.com
Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Possible telemetry exposure — immediate notice request

Hi Kimberly,

We detected an anomaly in our ingestion pipeline this morning that resulted in a limited set of telemetry events containing hashed identifiers that may map to user contact metadata. We believe the scope is small (approx 1,200 events across two ingestion shards) but some of the events appear to have been routed through one of Redwood's preprocessing subprocessors.

Under our DPA we have a 72-hour trigger for notification; legal has asked us to request confirmation of Redwood's preservation and initial triage plan. I've attached a forensic snapshot (forensic_snapshot_20270605.zip) and a filled privacy questionnaire with the fields we can share.

Can you confirm receipt and whether you will preserve relevant logs/artifacts and involve the subprocessor? We need an initial acknowledgement within 4 hours and a more detailed update within 24, followed by the consolidated notification within 72 hours if required.

Links and quick context: S3 bucket link (will send via secure channel) contains the sample export.

Thanks,
Jake Morris
CISO, FinLytics
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jake Morris <jake.morris@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible telemetry exposure — immediate notice request

Hi Jake — thanks for the alert and the snapshot. Confirming receipt of your message and the attached forensic snapshot. We will: 

- Immediately instruct the relevant subprocessor to preserve all incoming telemetry and VM-level snapshots.
- Create an incident workspace and preserve request/response logs for the two ingestion shards you flagged.
- Provide an initial technical triage update within 24 hours and a consolidated findings update within 72 hours per DPA obligations.

Ben, I’ve looped you in for triage. Marissa/Laura, please advise on legal/notification thresholds and whether we should prepare a proactive customer notice template. Jake — if you can share the secure S3 link (or Okta-approved transfer) and a small sample of event IDs, Ben can start correlation immediately.

Action items (initial):
- Jake: share secure link + sample IDs (ASAP).
- Ben: preserve and snapshot ingestion nodes; collect KV cache ranges.
- Marissa/Laura: confirm notification triggers under current DPA clauses and advise on subprocessor cooperation language to cite.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jake Morris <jake.morris@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible telemetry exposure — immediate notice request

Jake / team — quick technical notes from initial checks:  

- I see elevated error rates on ingestion shard-14 between 2027-06-05T02:10:00Z and 2027-06-05T03:45:00Z.
- Our preliminary logs show a small number of malformed JSON payloads that caused a fallback to legacy parsing; those fallbacks are where we think the hashed identifiers were preserved.

To triage we need: 1) the sample event IDs (min 3) and the object keys; 2) permission to temporarily mount the supplied S3 snapshot into our forensic environment (read-only). With that we can correlate hashes and enumerate any downstream copies.

I attached a short command checklist for our IR runbook (initial_command_list.txt) — we'll follow it and return a signed runbook entry. I can get first correlation results and a list of affected hostnames within 12–18 hours after we receive the snapshot.

Ben Carter
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Jake Morris <jake.morris@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finlytics.com
Date: 2027-06-05T12:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible telemetry exposure — immediate notice request

Ben — attaching the S3 transfer token via our secure channel (sent separately). The sample event IDs: FL-ev-00921, FL-ev-00922, FL-ev-00983. The attachment (forensic_snapshot_20270605.zip) contains the events and a README with object keys. 

We do not yet believe customer payloads were reconstructed into plaintext — this looks confined to hashed metadata fields that might be reversible with additional context. Regulators in our vertical have been explicit about timelines; legal is insisting on the 72-hour cadence.

Please confirm when you have read-only access and an ETA on the first correlation results.

Jake
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jake Morris <jake.morris@finlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible telemetry exposure — immediate notice request

Jake, Ben — thanks for the rapid collaboration. Legal guidance / next steps: 

- Based on the details provided, we will treat this as a limited-scope incident subject to the DPA notification clauses. Per clause 4.3 (Incident Notification) we will preserve and provide evidence, and we will aim to supply a consolidated technical summary suitable for your regulators within 72 hours.
- We will request the subprocessor cooperation letter and any statements we need to include in the notice; please expect a formal records request from our legal team within the hour.
- Our plan: initial technical update within 24 hours (ben: hostnames, ingress correlation, whether any downstream materialization occurred) and an operational/controls summary in the 72-hour package.

Jake — once Ben confirms read-only access, we will prepare a mutual action plan doc (link above) and share a draft disclosure template for your review. If either side needs to expedite to preserve regulatory options, call me directly.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
